A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 22-page versions of Mixed Signals. Their text, tables, figures, appendices A–C, and attached eight-page annotation specification support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original dataset analyses, detection experiments in Tables 3–4, and AB3DMOT tracking results in Appendix B.2/Table A2.

after.justification: v3 retains the original dataset analyses and detection/tracking experiments, including revised detection scores in Table 3.

M1.justification: The data-processing procedures and model adaptations are unchanged. Both versions describe PointPillar backbones, added 1-by-1 convolutional detection heads for three classes, and the same fusion implementations in Appendix A.1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Mixed Signals data for collaborative detection, detection enhanced by RSU communication, and preliminary tracking. The V2V4Real-to-Mixed Signals transfer scenario is also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 3–4 and the appendix tracking benchmark. V2V-AM receives a hyphen in its name; it remains the same cited comparator.

E3.justification: The scene splits, evaluation region, five-point visibility threshold, BEV IoU criteria, and fixed-RSU setting remain unchanged. Section 4.2 shortens the bandwidth explanation but retains averaging uncompressed message sizes. No protocol change is documented.

E4.justification: The alignment and annotation-quality comparisons, dataset distribution analyses, transfer visualization in Figure 11, and appendix intensity analysis are retained unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The numerical revisions introduce no change in uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 3 substantially revises the central detection benchmark under unchanged stated settings. Vehicle AP at IoU 0.5 changes from 0.17 to 0.42 for No Fusion, 0.71 to 0.82 for Attentive Fusion, and 0.59 to 0.43 for Late Fusion. The pedestrian AP at IoU 0.5 leader changes from Laly Fusion (0.62) to V2X-ViT (0.70, previously 0.54). Table 4, bandwidth values, and appendix tracking results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Task definitions, visibility criteria, and synchronization reasoning are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises mathematical assumptions, theorems, proofs, or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about dataset scale, heterogeneous LiDAR configurations, left-hand traffic, annotation quality, and benchmarking. Removing a generic closing aspiration does not alter the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning collaboration/bandwidth tradeoffs, transfer domain gaps, and EV visibility and intensity limitations remain substantively unchanged. Section 4.3.1 does not reconcile its blanket superiority statement with the revised Table 3 scores.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the chinitaberrio/Mixed-Signals reference with separate quan-dao/mixed-signals-devkit and acfr/Mixed-Signals-Dataset links. This changes documented code-access information; implementation, hardware, and annotation details are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, dataset positioning in Table 1, and all 48 cited works remain unchanged. Reference-list differences are pagination changes.

P1.justification: Limited edits shorten the bandwidth and domain-gap passages, trim the conclusion, adjust acknowledgements, standardize V2V-AM spelling, and clarify the devkit/code sentence. The section hierarchy and overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Figures and table structures are retained, with limited layout reflow. Section 4.3.2 moves to the bottom of the left column, the conclusion now fits on page 8, and appendix text and Table A3 shift within the existing layout.

improvement.justification: Separate devkit/code references make access information more explicit, but the PDFs do not explain whether the extensive Table 3 revisions correct errors or reflect other changes. The retained blanket superiority claim gains additional counterexamples: pedestrian AP at IoU 0.3 for V2V-Net versus No Fusion changes from 0.42 versus 0.25 to 0.42 versus 0.47. These documentation benefits and unresolved result-reliability concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
